eu1.evidence: The EU AI Act establishes a risk-based regulatory framework, classifying AI systems into four distinct tiers: Unacceptable Risk, High Risk, Limited Risk, Minimal Risk

eu2.evidence: High Risk: Systems subject to stringent obligations, including: Detailed technical documentation. Mandatory conformity assessments prior to EU market deployment.

eu3.evidence: Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces is broadly prohibited, with only three narrowly defined law enforcement exceptions: 1. Locating missing children or crime victims. 2. Preventing imminent terrorist threats or risks to life.

cyber1.evidence: Zero-Trust Architecture: Requires continuous verification of all users and devices, eliminating implicit trust based on network location

cyber2.evidence: MITRE ATT&CK Framework: Catalogs 14 tactical categories of adversary behavior, spanning the full attack lifecycle from initial access, execution, and privilege escalation to exfiltration and impact.

cyber3.evidence: Supply Chain Attacks: Incidents have surged by 742% between 2019 and 2022. Case in Point: The SolarWinds Orion compromise affected over 18,000 organizations worldwide, including US federal agencies

mkt1.evidence: Projected to reach $1.8 trillion by 2030, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 37% from 2023.

mkt2.evidence: Financial services lead multi-agent AI adoption, accounting for 34% of deployments, followed by healthcare and manufacturing.

mkt3.evidence: Companies deploying AI agents report a median 23% reduction in operational costs. However, these savings are offset by a 40% increase in infrastructure spending during the first 18 months of adoption

ir1.evidence: NIST Incident Response Lifecycle: Structures breach management into four phases: 1. Preparation 2. Detection and Analysis 3. Containment, Eradication, and Recovery 4. Post-Incident Activity

ir2.evidence: Breach Metrics (IBM, 2023): Mean time to identify a breach: 204 days. Mean time to contain a breach: 73 days.

ir3.evidence: Organizations with incident response (IR) teams and regularly tested IR plans saved an average of $2.66 million per breach.
